comments.body:
CONFIRMING EVIDENCE from Gerrit change 1577 (bug 85fa) — this is exactly the case in the title.

LLM-Review voted -1 with the bugfix-size-attestation finding: 321 non-test lines, over the
150-line bugfix floor, and bug 85fa had no plan-review attestation. I then EARNED the
attestation (rebar review-plan 85fa -> PASS, after correcting the ticket description). The
blocking condition was gone — but the vote could not be recomputed.

Four re-trigger paths, all swallowed by the copy condition
  ('changekind:NO_CODE_CHANGE OR changekind:MERGE_FIRST_PARENT_UPDATE OR TRIVIAL_REBASE'):
  1. git commit --amend --no-edit + push   -> same tree AND message -> NO_CODE_CHANGE -> copied
  2. commit-MESSAGE-only amend + push      -> tree unchanged        -> NO_CODE_CHANGE -> copied
  3. recheck-review comment                -> no reviewer response (see bug b0f5: fire-and-
                                              forget into a volatile queue) AND it cancelled
                                              the in-flight CI run (see bug 0d78)
  4. rebase onto current main + push       -> TRIVIAL_REBASE -> copied

CI behaves correctly by contrast — Verified re-ran on patch sets 3 and 4. Only the LLM review
is stuck, which makes the asymmetry easy to misread as 'the review just has not run yet'.

WHY THE COPY CONDITION IS WRONG FOR THIS FINDING SPECIFICALLY: bugfix-size-attestation's
evidence lives OUTSIDE the diff — it is attestation state on the TICKET. NO_CODE_CHANGE is a
sound reason to copy a finding about the CODE; it is unsound for a finding about the world
around the code, which can change without the tree changing. That distinction may be a
cleaner fix than making recheck-review special-case this one finding.

Cost observed: the change was unlandable on its own merits until a maintainer intervened, and
the detour also produced a spurious Verified -1 from the cancelled CI run.

(I filed 9b70 before finding this ticket — closing that as a duplicate of this one.)

compiled_state.description:
# `recheck-review` should accept a `bugfix-size-attestation` block once the ticket carries a current attestation

## The gap, hit for real

`retrigger.py:194` refuses `recheck-review` for ANY current-revision `finding` state, on the reasoning
that "the fix for a finding is amend + re-push, not a retry" (module docstring, `retrigger.py:15-19`).
That is right for a code veto. It is **wrong for `bugfix-size-attestation`**, whose remedy is not a code
change at all: the fix is to write the plan into the TICKET and run `rebar review-plan <id>`.

Observed on Gerrit change **1378** (bug `738a-376e-4829-42ca`):

```
[LLM-Review: BLOCK — finding]
rebar code review found 1 blocking issue(s):
- (bugfix-size-attestation) ... 162 non-test line(s) — over the 150-line floor for a bug fix — but
  bug 738a-376e-4829-42ca has no acceptable plan-review attestation (verdict: unsigned; ...)
```

The attestation was then earned (`review-plan 738a` -> PASS, signed; verified `certified` /
`valid: true`). The finding was therefore **stale**, but:

* `recheck-review` refused it as a "REAL FINDING";
* a no-code-change patchset **copies the -1 forward** (label copy condition
  `changekind:NO_CODE_CHANGE OR ... TRIVIAL_REBASE`), so re-pushing the same tree does not clear it.

So the only route was to invent a code change purely to force a re-review. That is exactly the
churn-for-the-bot the gate should never require, and it pressures a contributor into cosmetic edits to
an already-reviewed change.

## Why accepting this case is SAFE

The module's own security argument already covers it (`retrigger.py:15-19`): a re-review "can only
produce a fresh fail-closed verdict, never mint an unearned PASS". Refusing `finding` is a
churn-control measure, not a safety boundary. If the attestation is genuinely still missing, the fresh
review simply re-blocks.

## Design — both inputs stay PRIVILEGED-SIDE

The module's invariant is that eligibility is decided from durable Gerrit state, "never from anything
the requesting comment says" (`retrigger.py:13-14`). This condition honours that: it reads the **bot's
own** vote message plus the **ticket store**. Nothing from the requesting comment is consulted.

1. When the current state is `finding`, read the bot's own latest vote message on the current
   revision and require its HEADER count to be exactly one:
   `rebar code review found 1 blocking issue(s):`.

   **The header count is load-bearing and the finding LIST is not trustworthy for this.**
   `adapter.py:129-139` renders only the first **10** findings as `- (<criterion>) ...` lines and then
   appends `N additional blocking finding(s) omitted from this summary.` So "the rendered lines contain
   only bugfix-size-attestation" does NOT imply it is the only blocking finding — a mixed block could be
   unlocked by truncation. The header states the TOTAL (`len(blocking)`), so requiring exactly 1 closes
   that hole regardless of rendering. (Each finding's detail is also clipped at 240 chars,
   `adapter.py:133`, which is the second reason not to parse semantics out of the detail text.)
2. Require the single rendered `- (<criterion>)` line's criterion id to be exactly
   `bugfix-size-attestation`.
3. Resolve the ticket id from the CHANGE'S COMMIT MESSAGE via the gate's own resolver
   `ticket_for_commit_message(commit_message, repo_root=...)` — **not** from the finding text. This is
   how `apply_bugfix_size_gate` itself picks the ticket, so the two cannot disagree, and it sidesteps
   the 240-char detail clipping entirely rather than relying on the id happening to land inside it.
4. Re-classify with the gate's OWN privileged-side verifier,
   `bugfix_size_gate.classify_plan_review_attestation(ticket_id)` — the full chain (op-cert decode ->
   keyring verify at the storage anchor -> `compute_validity`) — and accept only when
   `bugfix_size_gate.bucket_for_verdict(verdict) == "accepted"`
   (`ACCEPTED_VERDICTS = {certified, stale-code, stale-head}`).
5. **Every failure path REFUSES** (fail-closed): header absent or count != 1, criterion line absent or
   not the expected id, commit message unavailable, ticket id unresolvable, classifier raising, or any
   non-`accepted` bucket. A parse that cannot establish the precondition is not evidence the
   precondition holds.

Reusing the gate's own classifier and bucketing is deliberate: a second, independent notion of
"acceptable attestation" in the retrigger path would drift from the gate that produced the finding.

## What must still refuse

* any block whose findings are not exactly `{bugfix-size-attestation}`;
* an attestation that is absent, `stale-material`, `mismatch`, `invalid`, or otherwise in
  `FLAG_VERDICTS` — otherwise a contributor could attest, then edit the plan, and unlock a re-review
  on an attestation that no longer covers the plan;
* an `infra` verdict (`unavailable` / `error`) must NOT auto-accept via this new arm — it is not
  evidence the attestation exists. (It remains eligible through the pre-existing coverage-gap arm if
  the bot itself tagged a coverage gap.)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `recheck-review` is ACCEPTED when the current revision's block is exactly the
      `bugfix-size-attestation` finding AND the named ticket's plan-review attestation buckets as
      `accepted` — proven RED-first, since the current code refuses every `finding`
- [x] a block containing `bugfix-size-attestation` PLUS any other blocking finding is still REFUSED
- [x] a `bugfix-size-attestation` block whose ticket attestation is absent or `stale-material` is
      still REFUSED, with the observed verdict named in the refusal reply
- [x] an `infra` verdict (`unavailable` / `error`) does not accept through this arm
- [x] eligibility reads only the bot's own vote message and the ticket store — asserted by a test that
      puts a forged criterion id and ticket id in the REQUESTING COMMENT and confirms it is ignored
- [x] the retrigger path still writes no vote (the existing no-`labels` invariant holds)
- [x] `classify_plan_review_attestation` / `bucket_for_verdict` are REUSED, not reimplemented —
      asserted by a test that monkeypatches the gate's classifier and observes the retrigger honour it
- [x] a block whose HEADER count is > 1 is REFUSED even when the only rendered `- (...)` line is
      `bugfix-size-attestation` — the truncation case, asserted with a synthetic 12-finding message
- [x] every parse failure refuses: missing header, unparseable count, missing criterion line,
      unresolvable ticket id, classifier exception — each asserted, not assumed
- [x] the ticket id comes from the commit-message trailer via `ticket_for_commit_message`, NOT from the
      finding detail text — asserted by a test whose finding text names a DIFFERENT ticket than the
      trailer, confirming the trailer wins
- [x] the refusal message for a genuine code finding is unchanged

## Testing

    pytest tests/unit -k "retrigger or recheck_review or bugfix_size" -q
    make lint && make typecheck

RED-first is load-bearing here: the accept path must be shown to fail against today's code (which
refuses every `finding`) before the condition is added, or the test proves nothing. The
forged-comment test is the security assertion — it is the one that would catch a future refactor that
starts trusting the requesting comment for the criterion id or the ticket id.
